decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard + Torkoal secures sun immediately, maximizing Fire-type damage and Solar Beam potential. Arbok provides Intimidate to soften physical threats and Sucker Punch priority to eliminate Archaludon. Mega Victreebel offers late-game cleanup with Innards Out after sun weakens checks.
decisions.notebook: Charizard-Mega-Y is the intended Mega for immediate Drought and Fire-type dominance. Sun enables Solar Beam turns and boosts Fire-type moves, critical for pressuring Water- and Steel-types like Rotom-Wash and Archaludon. Arbok's Sucker Punch is the only reliable tool to outspeed and KO Archaludon before it becomes unmanageable with Stamina. Toxapex remains a flexible pivot with Regenerator, but Victreebel's Mega evolution is prioritized for late-game sweep potential under sun. Always account for paralysis halving Arbok's Speed and prioritize eliminating Earthquake/Garchomp threats first.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash and Archaludon resist Fire and handle sun safely. Rotom pressures Torkoal with Hydro Pump, Archaludon Flash Cannons and Rock Slides Charizard-Y and Volcarona. Starmie and Garchomp provide speed and finishing power from back to clean up.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: vs sun cores, break sun early with Rotom/Starmie. Archaludon is primary win-con vs Grass/Poison, tanks with Stamina. Garchomp is fragile finisher, preserve HP. Cross-game: vs priority users (Sucker Punch), protect fragile Pokémon or go for KO before they act. Archaludon 1v1 vs physical attackers is winning matchup due to Def boosts and Leftovers. Paralyzed foes are less threatening but priority moves bypass speed. Flash Cannon is Archaludon's best STAB for hitting special-weak targets. Game 2: Sun team with Charizard-Y/Torkoal dual sun, Volcarona setup, Victreebel Chlorophyll. Lead Rotom/Archaludon to resist Fire and break sun. Starmie Thunderbolt pressures Charizard-Y. Garchomp Rock Slides Flying types from back.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving Charizard immediately secures Drought, enabling sun-boosted Fire moves and Solar Beam turns. Heat Wave pressures both foes, while Torkoal's Eruption threatens an OHKO on Archaludon and significant damage on Rotom-Wash. This line maximizes early-game pressure and sun utility, reducing the opponent's ability to pivot or set up.
decisions.notebook: Charizard-Mega-Y remains the intended Mega for sun dominance and Fire-type pressure. Sun enables Solar Beam turns and boosts Fire moves, critical for pressuring Water- and Steel-types. Archaludon's Stamina ability makes it a priority target to KO before it accumulates Defense boosts. Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump is a 4x weakness for Charizard, so scouting for it with Protect or eliminating it early is key. Arbok's Sucker Punch is reserved for late-game cleanup, especially against weakened Archaludon or Garchomp. Victreebel-Mega is prioritized for late-game sweeping under sun, leveraging Growth and Solar Beam.

decisions.rationale: Victreebel maintains sun and threatens Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam next turn. Torkoal survives Hydro Pump under sun (min 35% damage) and can retaliate with Earth Power. Arbok's Intimidate is less urgent than preserving Torkoal's bulk.
decisions.notebook: Sun dominance remains critical for Fire-type pressure and Solar Beam turns. Rotom-Wash is the immediate threat; eliminating it or forcing it out is prioritized. Victreebel-Mega is the late-game sweeper, so preserving it for endgame is ideal. Arbok's Sucker Punch is reserved for cleanup against weakened targets like Garchomp or Starmie. Torkoal's bulk and sun-boosted Eruption are key to maintaining offensive pressure. Stamina Archaludon is no longer a factor, but Garchomp's Rough Skin and Rock Slide/Earthquake must be accounted for in future turns.

decisions.rationale: Focus Charizard-Mega-Y with super effective attacks from both Pokémon. Rotom's Hydro Pump and Archaludon's Rock Slide can OHKO Charizard, removing the faster threat before it can sweep. Even if Charizard uses Solar Beam, Rotom has a chance to survive and attack, or Archaludon's Rock Slide will still hit Charizard. This applies maximum pressure and aims to break the sun core quickly.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Sun team with Charizard-Y/Torkoal dual sun, Volcarona setup, Victreebel Chlorophyll. Rotom-Wash is key to breaking sun with Fire/Ground resistance. Archaludon tanks physical hits with Stamina. Focus Charizard first as it outspeeds and threatens Rotom with Solar Beam. Preserve Rotom HP for later turns. Garchomp and Starmie are backup for Flying types and special sweeping.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp threatens Torkoal with super-effective Earthquake (54-114% with Life Orb) and pressures Volcarona/Victreebel with Rock Slide/Fire Fang. Bulkier than Starmie, can take hits. Rotom passes to preserve HP and pivot later with Volt Switch or burn with Will-O-Wisp. Garchomp + Rotom covers sun threats well.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Sun team (Charizard-Y/Torkoal dual sun, Volcarona setup, Victreebel Chlorophyll). Charizard-Y fainted turn 1 to Archaludon Rock Slide. Torkoal 73% with Heat Rock sun (8 turns). Rotom-Wash 56% HP, Sitrus consumed, Levitate blocks Ground. Archaludon fainted. Opponent remaining: Torkoal, Volcarona (Sitrus, Flame Body), Toxapex (Regenerator), Victreebel (Chlorophyll, can Mega), Arbok (Intimidate, Expert Belt). My remaining: Rotom-Wash, Garchomp (Life Orb, Jolly), Starmie (Wise Glasses, Timid, Analytic). Strategy: Break sun with Rotom/Garchomp, pressure setup sweepers. Garchomp key for Flying/Fire coverage.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is the highest priority threat. Solar Beam guarantees KO under sun, Earth Power secures it if Solar Beam misses. Eliminating Rotom now prevents Hydro Pump + Rock Slide/Earthquake from KOing Torkoal and severely damaging Victreebel. Sun dominance and offensive pressure are maximized.
decisions.notebook: Rotom-Wash elimination remains top priority due to its Hydro Pump threatening both Torkoal and Victreebel. Garchomp's Rough Skin and Rock Slide/Earthquake are secondary threats but cannot be ignored if Rotom is removed. Arbok's Sucker Punch is reserved for late-game cleanup against weakened Garchomp or Starmie. Victreebel-Mega is preserved for endgame sweeping under sun. Torkoal's bulk and sun-boosted Eruption are critical for maintaining offensive pressure. Future turns must account for Garchomp's Rough Skin damage on contact moves and potential Rock Slide flinches.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Victreebel outspeeds both my mons in sun and will Solar Beam Rotom (likely OHKO at 56%). Rotom Protects to survive, Garchomp Fire Fangs Victreebel for 38-90% damage. Torkoal's Earth Power only does 10-35% to Garchomp. This keeps both my mons alive, pressures Victreebel, and maintains momentum against sun team.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Sun team (Torkoal Drought HeatRock, Victreebel Chlorophyll). Charizard-Y fainted T1. Rotom 56% HP, Sitrus consumed. Archaludon fainted T1. Opponent remaining: Torkoal (73%), Victreebel (100%, can Mega to Innards Out), Volcarona (Sitrus, FlameBody), Toxapex (Regenerator), Arbok (Intimidate, ExpertBelt). My remaining: Rotom, Garchomp (LifeOrb, Jolly), Starmie (WiseGlasses, Timid, Analytic). Strategy: Break sun with Rotom/Garchomp, pressure setup sweepers. Garchomp key for Flying/Fire coverage. Victreebel outspeeds all in sun (180-244 Speed), must Protect Rotom or switch to avoid Solar Beam OHKO.

decisions.rationale: Rotom is the primary threat. Glare disables it, preventing Hydro Pump. Earth Power under sun secures KO, removing Rotom before it can threaten Torkoal or Arbok. Protect lines risk Garchomp Rock Slide flinches or Earthquake spread damage. Coil is premature without Rotom removed.
decisions.notebook: Rotom-Wash elimination remains top priority due to Hydro Pump's super-effective threat to Torkoal and Arbok. Garchomp's Rough Skin and Rock Slide/Earthquake are secondary but manageable if Rotom is removed first. Arbok's Sucker Punch is reserved for late-game cleanup against weakened Garchomp or Starmie. Torkoal's bulk and sun-boosted Eruption are critical for maintaining offensive pressure. Glare is a reliable tool to disable Rotom or Garchomp if needed. Victreebel-Mega is preserved for endgame sweeping under sun, but only after Rotom is eliminated. Future turns must account for Garchomp's Rough Skin on contact moves and potential Rock Slide flinches.

decisions.rationale: Focus fire on Torkoal to KO the sun setter. Rock Slide hits both foes (SE on Torkoal), Hydro Pump finishes Torkoal at 73%. Removing Drought is priority to prevent Volcarona setup and reduce Fire damage. Garchomp survives Arbok Sucker Punch with Rough Skin chip.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Sun team (Torkoal Drought HeatRock). Charizard-Y fainted T1, Victreebel fainted T2. Opponent remaining: Torkoal (73%), Arbok (100%, Intimidate used, ExpertBelt), Volcarona (Sitrus, FlameBody), Toxapex (Regenerator). My remaining: Rotom (56%, Sitrus consumed, -1 Atk), Garchomp (90%, LifeOrb, -1 Atk, Rough Skin), Starmie (100%, WiseGlasses, Analytic, Timid). Strategy: KO Torkoal to remove sun, then handle Arbok with Rotom/Garchomp. Starmie is strong switch-in vs Arbok (Ice Beam/Thunderbolt coverage). Garchomp key for Fire/Flying coverage vs Volcarona. Protect Rotom if sun persists to avoid Earth Power.

decisions.rationale: Glare Rotom-Wash is safest: blocks Hydro Pump, forces Garchomp to Earthquake into Arbok’s bulk (80-95% range) or Rock Slide (45-55%), preserving Arbok for Starmie/Blaziken later. Poison Jab risks Hydro Pump KO, Sucker Punch fails vs Protect. Rotom elimination remains priority.
decisions.notebook: Rotom-Wash is the linchpin threat: Hydro Pump OHKOs Arbok after minimal chip, and its Protect + Will-O-Wisp disrupts physical attackers. Garchomp’s Earthquake is secondary but lethal if Rotom is removed first. Glare is the most reliable tool to neutralize Rotom’s offensive presence, while Sucker Punch is reserved for cleanup. Victreebel-Mega’s endgame sweep is contingent on Rotom’s removal and sun maintenance. Future leads must account for Starmie’s Ice Beam and Blaziken’s Speed Boost, but Rotom remains the immediate obstacle. Preserve Arbok’s bulk for late-game Sucker Punch KOs on weakened foes.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp Earthquake is a possible OHKO (91-221%) vs Arbok even at -1 Atk with Life Orb spread reduction. Rotom Protect avoids friendly Earthquake damage and blocks any Arbok attack. Sucker Punch only does 9-25% to Garchomp, so Garchomp survives and fires first after priority. If EQ doesn't KO, Arbok is at ≤8% and dies to any follow-up.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Sun team (Torkoal Drought). Charizard-Y fainted T1, Victreebel fainted T2, Torkoal fainted T3. Opponent remaining: Arbok (Expert Belt, Intimidate used), Volcarona (Sitrus, FlameBody), Toxapex (Regenerator). My remaining: Rotom (56%, no item, -1 Atk), Garchomp (81%, LifeOrb, -1 Atk, Rough Skin), Starmie (100%, WiseGlasses, Analytic, Timid). Strategy: KO Arbok with Garchomp Earthquake, then handle Volcarona/Toxapex. Starmie is strong switch-in vs Arbok (Ice Beam/Thunderbolt coverage, resists Poison Jab). Garchomp key for Fire/Flying coverage vs Volcarona. Rotom can burn physical threats with Will-O-Wisp.

reflections.summary: Lost due to team-preview mismatch: the sun core (Charizard-Y + Torkoal) was hard-countered by Rotom-Wash, which survived the lead Eruption, Protect-stalled, and OHKOed both sun setters with Hydro Pump. The intended Victreebel sweep never materialized because Rotom remained healthy and Garchomp cleaned up afterward.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Torkoal with a sun-compatible Pokémon that can pressure Rotom-Wash (e.g., Venusaur-Mega or Volcarona) to prevent Rotom from freely stalling and attacking.
reflections.notebook: Rotom-Wash is the linchpin: survives sun leads, Protect-stalls, OHKOs sun setters with Hydro Pump, and spreads burns. Garchomp’s Earthquake is secondary but lethal if Rotom is removed. Starmie’s Ice Beam threatens Charizard-Y and Victreebel; Blaziken’s Speed Boost outspeeds everything post-Mega. Future leads must either remove Rotom immediately or bring a sun partner that can pressure it (e.g., Venusaur-Mega). Glare remains the best Rotom answer; preserve Arbok for late-game Sucker Punch cleanup.

reflections.summary: The team preview of Rotom-Wash, Archaludon, Garchomp, and Starmie perfectly dismantled the opponent's sun core. Archaludon's Rock Slide immediately KO'd Mega Charizard-Y on Turn 1, removing the primary win condition before it could act. Garchomp's Fire Fang removed Chlorophyll Victreebel on Turn 2, and the Rotom-Wash/Garchomp combination cleaned up Torkoal and Arbok by Turn 4. The sun strategy was neutralized before it could generate momentum.
reflections.adjustment: For Game 3, anticipate the opponent may pivot to Volcarona and Toxapex instead of the sun core. If Charizard-Y is not brought, Archaludon's primary value (Rock Slide snipe) diminishes—consider replacing it with additional speed or coverage. Lead with Garchomp to immediately threaten Volcarona with Rock Slide, and use Rotom-Wash's Will-O-Wisp to neuter physical threats or pivot with Volt Switch for momentum.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster: Charizard-Y (Modest, CharizarditeY, HeatWave/AirSlash/SolarBeam/Protect), Torkoal (Quiet, HeatRock, Drought, Eruption/HeatWave/EarthPower/Protect), Victreebel (Modest, Victreebelite, Chlorophyll, SolarBeam/SludgeBomb/Growth/Protect), Arbok (Jolly, ExpertBelt, Intimidate, PoisonJab/SuckerPunch/Glare/Coil), Volcarona (Timid, SitrusBerry, FlameBody, QuiverDance/FieryDance/BugBuzz/Protect), Toxapex (Calm, Leftovers, Regenerator, Surf/ToxicSpikes/Haze/Recover). Game 2: Opponent led Charizard-Y + Torkoal; Archaludon Rock Slide OHKO'd Charizard-Y T1, Garchomp Fire Fang OHKO'd Victreebel T2, Rotom+Garchomp cleaned remaining sun. Sun core is highly vulnerable to immediate Rock Slide pressure on Charizard-Y and Fire coverage on Victreebel. Volcarona and Toxapex remain untested; expect Volcarona to attempt Quiver Dance setup and Toxapex to stall with Regenerator. Rotom-Wash + Garchomp core is proven effective for closing games against this team.
